content: If someone experiences severe symptoms such as losing consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. For other cases, contact a poison control center without delay. In the United States, you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, you can call 1-844-764-7669. Before starting this medication and during its use, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as a G6PD blood test and blood cell counts, should be conducted. It is essential to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in May 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before taking primaquine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, using machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. Primaquine may cause a condition that affects heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood may also increase your risk of QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you use certain drugs (such as diuretics or water pills) or have conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This medication must not be used during pregnancy as it may harm an unborn baby. Women of childbearing age should undergo a pregnancy test before starting this medication. It is crucial to prevent pregnancy during and after treatment with primaquine. Both men and women must use reliable forms of birth control (such as condoms or birth control pills) during treatment. Men should continue using birth control for at least three months after the end of treatment, and women should continue for at least one menstrual cycle after the end of treatment. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. If you are pregnant, traveling to an area with malaria significantly increases the risk of death and other complications for both you and your infant. The CDC recommends continuing other malaria treatments (such as chloroquine) throughout pregnancy until delivery to prevent harm to your unborn baby (e.g., hemolytic anemia). After delivery, you may complete treatment with primaquine. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk. Your doctor should test your infant for G6PD deficiency before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away.
